full_judgment:
Mr. A. K. Badrul Huq, J: By this application the defendant-petitioner of Civil Revision Case seeks for an order dispensing with the direction recorded by this court to file the decree of the Family Court. 

 4. In the Civil Revision Petition, decree of the courts below had not been filed and the learned Advocate appearing for the plaintiff petitioner undertook to file the certified copies of the decrees of the courts below within two (2) weeks. Accordingly, at the time of issuance of Rule the plaintiff petitioner was directed to file the decrees of the courts below within two (2) weeks from date in the section. In default, the rule was to stand discharged. 

 5. On 7.12.1999 the plaintiff petitioner had only filed the decree recorded by the Family Appellate Court in Family Appeal No. 56 of 1997 in the section vide Entry No. 47928 dated 5.12.1999. But the decree of the Family Court in Family Suit No. 8 of 1995 had not been filed within the time fixed by this court. 

 6. Thereafter, an application for dispensing with the direction to file the decree of the Family Court was registered on 6.12.1999 and affidavit had been also shown on that date i.e. on 6.12.1999 which was after the expiry of the period fixed by the court. On 5.12.1999 the period of two (2) weeks expired. The said application was presented before the court on 3.1.2000 and the same appeared in the list on 4.1.2000, and on that date at the instance of the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner the matter was adjourned for two weeks. 

 8. In the application registered on 6.12.1999 it had been stated that the petitioner applied for the certified copies of both the decrees and got the decree of the appellate court and on query came to know that the decree of the trial court had not been drawn up and being asked the concerned Sheristadar informed that decrees are not drawn up for the cases of the minors and as of the decree of the trial court. The petitioner thus this is, prayed for disposing with the direction to file the decree of the Family Court. 

 9. Section 16(1) of the Family Court Ordinance, 1985 enjoins that a Family Court shall pass a decree in such form and manner and shall enter its particulars in such register of decrees prescribed. 

 10. Rule 5 of the Family Court Rules, 1985 mandates that in every suit under the Ordinance on passing the judgment, a decree shall be drawn up in form C and shall be signed by the presiding Judge, and the decree shall bear the seal of the Family Court. 

 11. Sub-section 1 of section 17 of the Ordinance enshrines that subject to the provisions of sub-section 2, an appeal shall lie from a judgment, decree or order of Family Court to the Court of District Judge. Sub-section 5 of section 17 states that .a certified copy of the judgment, decree or order of the court from which the appeal is preferred shall be attached with the appeal. 

 13. From the above it has, thus, been manifestly clear that a decree will be drawn up by the Family Court after the pronouncement of the judgment. 

 14. On 21.11.1999 at the time of issuance of Rule this court directed the plaintiff-petitioner to file decrees of both the courts below within two (2) weeks from date in the section with the default clause that Rule would stand discharged in the event of non-compliance of the order. The order is quoted hereunder: 

 "The plaintiff-petitioner is directed to file the decrees of both the courts below within 2 (two) weeks from date in the section, in default, the Rule shall stand discharged." 

 16. On 4.1.2000 the matter was adjourned for two (2) weeks on the basis of a prayer made by the learned Advocate for the plaintiff petitioner. There was no scope for recording any further order on the matter after recording the positive order dated 21.11.1999 that the rule would stand discharged in default of filing the decree of courts below within two (2) weeks from date. This order dated 4:1.2000 appears to have been passed under misapprehension and the said order is hereby re-called. 

 17. On conspectus, I am of this positive view that this court after recording the order dated 21.11.1999 got no scope for passing any order dispensing with the order directing the plaintiff petitioner to file the decree of the trial court in the section. This application, thus, stands rejected and the rule issued on 21.11.1999, also, stands discharged for default.
